page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-1 is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n1 server family. It features 1 dedicated vCPU mapped to 1 physical core and 1 thread, running on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local storage or bundled GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tier of cloud compute resources. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1088.79 is categorized as weak, while the multi-core score of 1088.79 falls into the poor category. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 10.68 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 9.71 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10% of tested systems. Geekbench scores reflect similar constraints, with a single-core score of 895.0 and a multi-core score of 898.0.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-1 offers a low-cost entry point for basic cloud hosting but delivers low performance-per-resource. It supports basic CPU instructions like AVX, AES, and FMA, but lacks newer extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX. This hardware profile is best suited for lightweight, non-demanding workloads such as basic static web serving, small utility scripts, development testing, or simple background tasks that do not require high memory bandwidth or multi-threaded processing.
